_comment: AI radar source catalog. Three groups. ENGINEERING CORE (12 sources, the largest and the reason the radar exists): LangGraph and agent frameworks, harness engineering, context engineering, prompt engineering, MCP, agent memory, guardrails, evals, tool use, and the coding agents themselves. PRIMARY, chosen by the user: labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), the people building them, investors, and NVIDIA. SUPPORTING press and research, because the primary tier cannot report on itself -- the labs announce but do not analyse, the people publish on X which has no fetchable feed, and the VC firms blog about portfolio companies rather than deals. Fields: id, name, feed (RSS/Atom; null when the source publishes none - read 'site' with WebFetch, or set 'sitemap'), site, lang (also decides the card's language), category, weight (1-5). Optional: topic_filter, topic_terms, topic_exclude, max_items, kind, note. Validated against the live network on 2026-09-03. Do NOT add github.com releases.atom feeds: the cloud sandbox scopes GitHub access to the cloned repository and returns 403 for every other repo.

sources.name: Anthropic News
sources.note: No public RSS (11 paths checked 2026-09-03, all 404). Read via the sitemap, which carries /news/ URLs with lastmod dates. Titles come from the URL slug and have no summary, so read the page before writing a card.

sources.name: Andrej Karpathy
sources.note: Posts far more often on X, which has no fetchable feed. This blog is low volume.

sources.name: Boris Cherny
sources.note: Claude Code. Low volume; most output is on X, which cannot be fetched.

sources.name: Thariq Shihipar
sources.note: Claude Code. Low volume; most output is on X, which cannot be fetched.

sources.name: The Batch (Andrew Ng / DeepLearning.AI)
sources.note: Andrew Ng's weekly letter plus DeepLearning.AI's news roundup. No RSS (/feed/, /rss.xml and /the-batch/rss.xml all 404 on 2026-09-03); read via the sitemap, which carries full timestamps. andrewng.org is not a separate source: it publishes no feed and no sitemap, and the letters land here. Titles come from the URL slug and have no summary, so read the page before writing a card.

sources.name: Sam Altman
sources.note: Personal blog. Rare but high-signal; his frequent posting is on X.

sources.name: Andreessen Horowitz
sources.note: No RSS at any conventional path (checked 2026-09-03). Read via post-sitemap.xml, which carries lastmod dates. Titles come from the URL slug and have no summary.

sources.name: NVIDIA Blog
sources.note: NVIDIA's own name is a topic keyword, so the global filter passes everything. The exclusion drops its gaming beat, which is most of the feed.

sources.name: NVIDIA Newsroom
sources.note: NVIDIA's own name is a topic keyword, so the global filter passes everything. The exclusion drops its gaming beat, which is most of the feed.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.note: Carries the funding, valuation and M&A news the VC blogs do not.

sources.name: The Decoder
sources.note: Highest signal per item. Reports what the lab founders say, which their own feeds do not.

sources.name: Ars Technica AI
sources.note: Depth and scepticism; strongest on legal and policy.

sources.name: Latent Space
sources.note: Agentic coding coverage. Editorial stand-in for the GitHub release feeds, which the cloud sandbox blocks.

sources.name: Anthropic Engineering
sources.note: The canonical source for the agenda this radar exists for: context engineering, harness design, agent skills, advanced tool use, Claude Code internals. Same sitemap as the anthropic entry, filtered to /engineering/ instead of /news/. Roughly one post a month -- silent most days, and worth a HIGH card when it fires.

sources.name: LangChain Blog
sources.note: LangGraph, LangSmith, MCP integration and agent memory -- the only source in the catalog covering that stack directly. Webflow site, no RSS: read from www.langchain.com/sitemap.xml. CAVEAT: the sitemap bulk-stamps lastmod on a site rebuild -- 92 posts over 30 days carried only 23 distinct timestamps, one cluster of 21. Hence max_items 4 and the exclusion of newsletters and customer stories. If a day shows four LangChain items with the same date, check the post itself before writing a card.

sources.name: Simon Willison
sources.note: Daily hands-on practice with Claude Code, Codex and every new model. The ai-assisted-programming tag feed exists but carries only 4 posts in 30 days; the everything feed carries 26, so it is read with the topic gate instead.

sources.name: GitHub AI & ML Blog
sources.note: Copilot practice and evaluation writeups from the team that ships it -- 90% of its posts land on this radar's agenda. Complements github-changelog, which carries the platform changes.

sources.name: InfoQ AI, ML & Data Engineering
sources.note: Production practice: context engineering, prompt compression, agent architecture. Edited for engineers rather than for the AI press cycle.

sources.name: Hugging Face Blog
sources.note: Agent memory, structured outputs, fine-tuning and evaluation, with runnable code. Mixed with model-release posts, hence the topic gate.

sources.name: Cursor Changelog
sources.note: A coding agent the teams may use, and the only agent changelog reachable from the sandbox -- GitHub releases.atom is 403 for every repo but the cloned one. Entries are named by feature, not by version, so kind: release is not set.

sources.name: Zed Blog
sources.note: Editor and agent-panel work. Two posts in 30 days; silent most days, on-topic when it fires.

sources.name: Sourcegraph Blog
sources.note: Amp and code-search-driven agents. Low volume, high on-topic rate.

sources.name: Martin Fowler
sources.note: Practice writing on LLMs in software teams, from the person the audience already reads on everything else. Topic-gated because the feed also carries general architecture writing.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog
sources.note: Covers all of GitHub, so it needs a gate. Uses its own vocabulary: the global filter dropped 'Enterprise-managed settings support any default model', a real Copilot governance change.
